items.title: Hardeep Singh Puri to be back in Parliament: Epstein files forgotten
items.summary: Look at this photograph. Hardeep Singh Puri, now India’s Petroleum Minister, sitting across a table from Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who counted some of the world’s most powerful people among his associates. Puri says he met Epstein only three or four times, as part of official delegations. That gets demolished with this photo. And emails and other records suggest a more extensive relationship. And this goes beyond Epstein. Puri spent decades as a diplomat, moving through the world of global think tanks, billionaires and influential power brokers, long before he joined the Union Cabinet. Despite all the outrage, Puri has just been renominated to the Rajya Sabha by the BJP. So, who is Hardeep Singh Puri, and how did he build this network of access? items.title: CJI Surya Kant inaugurates Jharkhand High Court’s data centre, stresses need to protect judicial records
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday inaugurated the Jharkhand High Court’s data centre. Speaking at the event, he stressed the need to protect sensitive judicial records against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. “Judicial records contain sensitive information and must be protected against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. Cybersecurity, reliable backup arrangements, regular testing and trained technical personnel are essential to maintaining public confidence in digital systems,” he stated. The data centre project represents an investment of approximately ₹25 crore. Its value, the CJI noted, would be measured by improvements in court functioning and the experience of litigants, rather than the equipment installed. The event also marked the launch of the High Court’s new website, an online certified copy application for civil courts across Jharkhand, a personalised cause list and Dragon speech-to-text software. Highlighting their practical benefits, the CJI explained that the online certified copy facility would reduce unnecessary travel and expense for litigants, while the personalised cause list would help advocates locate cases and prepare for hearin

items.title: Rajasthan High Court restores separate registration of criminal writ petitions; overrules former acting CJ's verdict
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court full bench on Monday held that writ petitions arising from criminal matters must be registered separately as criminal writ petitions [Ravi Kumar v State Of Rajasthan & Ors.] . A Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay K Agrawal , Justice Sameer Jain and Justice Anuroop Singhi overruled an earlier verdict rendered in this regard by a division bench headed by former acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma. The full bench observed that the July 2026 division bench ruling of the Court had failed to consider Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, which requires writ petitions arising from criminal matters to be registered separately. "The aforesaid decision in Jiya failed to consider or give effect to the statutory mandate embodied in Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, its ratio, insofar as it prohibits criminal-side registration of such writ applications, is held to be per incuriam, having been rendered in ignorance of, or without due consideration of, a relevant statutory provision," held the full bench.
